content:
This case concerns the judicial division of a holiday villa in Condofuri Marina, purchased by a couple during their marriage under the legal community regime. Following their separation in 2017, the husband sought to dissolve the co-ownership, while the wife contested the division and filed a claim for damages, alleging that the husband had enjoyed exclusive use of the property, effectively barring her access.
The Court first clarified that upon legal separation, the marital community dissolves, and the asset shifts into the regime of ordinary co-ownership. A Court-Appointed Expert (CTU) determined that the property, valued at €98,800, was not conveniently divisible into two autonomous units due to its modest size and the structural limitations of having only one bathroom. During the proceedings, the parties eventually agreed on the assignment of the entire property to the husband, provided he paid the wife her 50% share (€49,400),.
Crucially, the Court dismissed the wife’s claim for occupancy indemnity as procedurally inadmissible. Under Italian civil procedure (Art. 167 CPC), a counterclaim for damages must be filed at least 20 days before the first hearing; because the wife filed her defense only eight days prior, she forfeited her right to pursue those damages within this specific trial.
